programmes.name_en: Irish Research and Development (R&D) Corporation Tax Credit
programmes.amount_note: 30% of qualifying R&D expenditure for accounting periods commencing on or after 1 January 2024 (previously 25%). The credit is repaid in three annual instalments; for each instalment the company elects whether it is treated as an overpayment, offset against tax liabilities, or repaid in cash. No cap on qualifying expenditure.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed in the corporation tax return; claims must generally be made within 12 months of the end of the accounting period.

procedure_steps.detail: Confirm the activities meet the statutory definition of qualifying R&D and record qualifying expenditure.

programmes.amount_note: A qualifying company can raise up to EUR 5.5 million a year and EUR 16.5 million in its lifetime. Investors get income tax relief on their investment, making the round easier to raise. Per Revenue, the scheme is now called the Employment Investment Incentive (EII); an individual investor can claim relief on up to €500,000 a year (shares held 7 years) or €250,000 a year (held 4 years) for shares issued after 2019.

eligibility.other_note: Self-assessed by the company - there is no advance approval, so professional advice is essential. Shares must be held for at least four years by the investor.

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum investment on which you can claim relief in a year is: ... €500,000 in respect of the years after 2019, subject to those shares being held for a minimum period of seven years

programmes.amount_note: Refundable credit on qualifying R&D expenditure. The rate was increased to 30% (from 25%) for accounting periods beginning on or after 1 January 2024. Payable in three instalments, or in full in year one below a first-year payment threshold.
programmes.deadline_note: Claimed with the corporation tax return; the claim must be made within 12 months of the end of the accounting period in which the expenditure was incurred - a hard deadline with no extension.

procedure_steps.detail: Identify qualifying R&D activities under the science and technology test
Track qualifying expenditure (staff, materials, plant, subcontracting within limits)
Prepare technical and financial documentation contemporaneously
File the claim with the CT1 return within 12 months of the period end
Revenue may raise queries or audit

documents_required.doc: Technical report describing the scientific or technological uncertainty and advance

eligibility.other_note: The single most valuable non-dilutive support for Irish R&D startups because it is refundable in cash even when loss-making. The 12-month claim deadline is strict. Grant funding must be deducted from qualifying expenditure.

programmes.source_snippet: For accounting periods commencing on or after 1 January 2024, the rate has increased to 30%. ... repaid in three annual instalments.

programmes.name_local: Start-up companies relief from corporation tax (Section 486C)
programmes.name_en: Start-up companies relief from corporation tax (Section 486C)
programmes.amount_note: Reduction of Corporation Tax for the first five years of trading. Full relief where total CT due is €40,000 or less in a year; marginal relief where CT is between €40,000 and €60,000. Relief is limited to €5,000 employer's PRSI per employee or director (Class S: €1,000 per individual from 2025), with an overall limit of €40,000 qualifying PRSI per accounting period. Unused relief can be carried forward.

eligibility.other_note: Claimed in the corporation tax return. Only relevant once profitable, but it can be carried forward if unused in the first five years.

programmes.source_snippet: You may be entitled to relief if your total CT due is €40,000 or less in a tax year. If your CT due is between €40,000 and €60,000, you may be entitled to partial relief.

programmes.amount_note: Refund of PAYE income tax paid over the previous six years, invested into your own new company. Refund can be up to around EUR 140,000 depending on prior tax paid (up to EUR 100,000 per year invested).

eligibility.other_note: For employees, unemployed or recently redundant people starting their own business: must establish a new company with a new qualifying trade, have mainly PAYE income in the previous four years, take up full-time employment in the company as director or employee, invest cash for new shares and hold them at least four years. Claims are made to Revenue's EII branch.

programmes.source_snippet: SURE is a tax relief that provides a refund of Income Tax that you paid in previous years.

programmes.name_local: Screen Ireland / Fís Éireann development funding
programmes.name_en: Screen Ireland development and production funding
programmes.amount_note: Feature Film Development Loans: maximum €75,000 without match funding, up to €125,000 with third-party match funding; awards well below the maximum are likely. Loans are repayable on the first day of principal photography (with a 'locked box' re-investment pilot for Irish feature films). Other development strands (TV drama, documentary, animation, screenplay) have their own limits.
programmes.deadline_note: Schemes have individual deadlines published on the Screen Ireland funding pages; some development funding is assessed on a rolling basis.

eligibility.other_note: Irish feature film strand: independent production companies registered in the Republic of Ireland with an office and staff there, with rights access and an agreement in principle with the screenwriter.

programmes.source_snippet: The maximum amount available is €75,000 without match funding. A maximum of €125,000 may be awarded with third party match funding from other sources.

programmes.name_local: SEAI Research, Development and Demonstration Fund
programmes.name_en: SEAI Research, Development and Demonstration Fund
programmes.amount_note: Supports energy RD&D projects. Awards have ranged from tens of thousands for feasibility to around EUR 1 million for demonstration projects; grant rates follow State aid limits.
programmes.deadline_note: 2026 call opened 13 May 2026 and closed at 13:00 on Tuesday 30 June 2026; award notification Q4 2026. Next call date not announced.

eligibility.other_note: Open to companies, research organisations and public bodies in Ireland. Projects must have a clear Irish energy system benefit.

programmes.source_snippet: SEAI National Energy Research Funding Call - 2026 Call Now Closed ... Application Submission Deadline 13:00 (Irish Standard Time) Tuesday 30th June 2026

programmes.name_local: Research Ireland (SFI) Frontiers for the Future
programmes.name_en: Research Ireland (SFI) Frontiers for the Future
programmes.amount_note: Award amount €600,000 - €1,500,000 (direct costs) over 4 to 5 years; budgets above €1,000,000 need prior approval from Research Ireland.
programmes.deadline_note: Deadline listed as 'Rolling'; apply through SESAME. Awards run 4 to 5 years.

eligibility.other_note: Research funding (now Research Ireland, formerly SFI): applicants must be independent researchers hosted by an eligible Research Body, with a PhD for at least 3 years and senior authorship on at least 3 international peer-reviewed articles. Not open to companies directly; postdocs not eligible.

programmes.source_snippet: Deadline Rolling ... Award amount €600,000 - €1,500,000 (direct costs)

programmes.amount_note: Up to €130,000 in direct costs (eligible salary or teaching buy-out, travel and training, open access publishing), including a fixed €10,000 travel and training budget. Fellowships last 1-12 months full-time or up to 24 months part-time. Industry Partners contribute in-kind.
programmes.deadline_note: Industry Fellowship call launched 30 September 2026; applications open on SESAME 12 October 2026. Batches assessed at deadlines of 19 November 2026, 31 March 2027 and 30 September 2027 (13:00 Irish time); further dates to be added.

eligibility.other_note: Replaces the earlier Industry RD&I Fellowship. Applicant is a researcher (faculty, postdoc or late-stage PhD) backed by an Irish Research Body and a single nominated Industry Partner (a company in Ireland or abroad). Fellow works mainly at the company. Public bodies cannot be the Industry Partner.

programmes.source_snippet: Research Ireland provides up to a maximum of €130,000 in direct costs ... Applications can be submitted at any time, but batches of applications will be assessed at the following assessment deadlines: 19th November 2026

programmes.amount_note: Údarás offers capital, employment, feasibility, R&D, training and equity supports, plus smaller schemes such as the TAME grant (50% up to €2,500). Amounts for the main grants are not published on the page and are set per project within EU State aid limits. The 2026 Gaeltacht Tourism Pilot (up to €50,000 at 50% or 75%) had a deadline of 30 June 2026 and has passed.
programmes.deadline_note: Rolling applications through an Udaras regional office.

procedure_steps.detail: Contact your regional Udaras na Gaeltachta office
Discuss the project and eligibility with a development executive
Submit a business plan and grant application
Board approval
Draw down against evidenced spend

eligibility.other_note: The business must be located in a Gaeltacht area (parts of Donegal, Mayo, Galway, Kerry, Cork, Meath and Waterford). Udaras is the enterprise agency for these areas in place of Enterprise Ireland and the LEOs, and also operates gteic digital hubs.

programmes.source_snippet: Capital grants can be paid for initial investment in material and immaterial assets. ... The €2,500 (50% of eligible expenditure) grant contributes to export research and marketing costs
